speakers: Yoav Git (co-host, Gresham, fixed income trend manager and researcher)
summary: Yoav Git and Niels Kaastrup-Larsen discuss early-2026 trends (Japan yields, gold, natural gas, EM FX) and Git's ERAS paper: bonds fail in rising inflation, commodity trend is the mirror image, and a 50/50 mix gives CPI+4% in all regimes. They also review Rob Carver's blog on carry and autocorrelation.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: we as investors, we need to imagine the unimaginable um and that focusing on building robust portfolios that may not give you the highest returns
claims.claim: Given geopolitical breakdown (Greenland, loss of trust), investors should build robust portfolios that get through the next five to seven years safely rather than maximise return.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: I believe this can only be done by combining truly uncorrelated strategies and assets
claims.claim: Robustness comes only from combining truly uncorrelated strategies and assets.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: we may see many many unimaginable moves in the coming years
claims.claim: A breakdown in world order (a fourth turning) could create huge moves in financial markets, as already seen in commodities, which is an opportunity for trend following.
claims.conditions: if the world order really breaks down

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: for longerterm managers um that don't react on every single news item, it's probably been an okay week
claims.claim: In a headline-driven week, long-term trend managers fared okay; results depended on exposure to gold, silver, equities and JGBs.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: this last week net gas futures up 71%
claims.claim: Natural gas futures jumped 71% in a week on a US cold front, a non-geopolitical supply and demand shock of the kind commodity trends form on.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: Japan where yields really spiked up and suddenly we had 10ear JDBs at 241
claims.claim: Japanese 10-year yields spiked to about 2.41% in a mini Truss moment, a big move in JGBs and the yen versus the 7% of the 1990s.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: in the case of gold it's really the breakdown of uh the breakdown of trust in in fiat currencies
claims.claim: Gold's rise reflects loss of trust in fiat currencies (Dalio says to hold gold), while other commodities move for different reasons.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: my trend barometer is picking up um a little bit of uh better conditions
claims.claim: The Trend Barometer finished at 50, a reasonably strong reading; as of Tuesday January 2026 BTOP50 +3.18%, SG CTA +3.46%, SG Trend +3.78%, short-term traders +1.07%, MSCI World +1.5%, S&P total return +0.5%.

claims.speaker: Yoav Git
claims.quote: there are a lot of trends everywhere so FX um FX EMFX has been very very good
claims.claim: Early 2026 had trends in many places, including Japan, the Taiwan dollar, rates, the Turkish lira, and emerging market FX did very well.
claims.indicator: EM FX, Taiwan dollar, Turkish lira

claims.speaker: Yoav Git
claims.quote: once the the gap between Japanese yields and US yield is closing it becomes actually better to that carry trade is kind of disappearing and you you see flows from US bonds back into Japan
claims.claim: As Japanese yields rise toward US yields, the carry trade fades and money returns from US bonds to Japan, which pressures the US market (10-year crossing 4.2%).

claims.speaker: Yoav Git
claims.quote: each country becoming more interested in securing its own supply chain
claims.claim: A breakdown of trust makes countries prioritise secure supply chains and more spending (military), sacrificing efficiency, which is inflationary and part of the secular move away from globalisation (Bill White).

claims.speaker: Yoav Git
claims.quote: it takes 20 years to build a mine and that that sort of uh impact basically means that price needs to do a lot of trend
claims.claim: The transition from a carbon to a metal economy and the 20-year lag to build a mine mean price must adjust, producing trends in commodities.

claims.speaker: Yoav Git
claims.quote: we tend to think about inflation as being driven by demand by just too much money chasing too few goods. Uh but actually it's a lot of it is at the moment it's being supply
claims.claim: Current inflation is largely supply-driven (gas from Russia, compromised supply chains) rather than demand-driven.

claims.speaker: Yoav Git
claims.quote: how does an allocator approach the problem of constructing a portfolio which will be robust in all weathers
claims.claim: The ERAS tool defines inflation regimes (high, rising, low, falling) to build an all-weather allocation that is consistent across inflation periods, since bonds are the worry.

claims.speaker: Yoav Git
claims.quote: it will give you 0% essentially 0% in high inflation environments
claims.claim: Equities return about CPI+0 in high inflation (real return zero), about CPI+10-15 in low inflation, and a little in between.
claims.indicator: real equity return by inflation regime

claims.speaker: Yoav Git
claims.quote: once you start looking at rising inflation, bonds start to underperform. They don't they no longer give you CPI plus, they start giving you CPI minus
claims.claim: In rising inflation bonds return CPI minus, and at about 4.5% inflation they are strongly negative and more correlated with equities, so they fail as the building block.
claims.indicator: real bond return by inflation regime

claims.speaker: Yoav Git
claims.quote: commodities ities act as almost the negative the the mirror image of what bonds are in a sense
claims.claim: Commodities mirror bonds: they do very well in inflation and very poorly in low inflation.

claims.speaker: Yoav Git
claims.quote: commodity trend actually is a great strategy for both inflationary times for the obvious reasons like what we see at the moment but also during low inflation times it has a little bit less drag
claims.claim: Commodity trend works in inflationary periods and drags less in low inflation (a little less negative carry) than long-only commodities.

claims.speaker: Yoav Git
claims.quote: a portfolio like simply a 50% commodities 50% bonds you get something which is truly all weather
claims.claim: A 50% bonds, 50% commodity trend portfolio gives roughly CPI+4% in every inflation environment with little equity correlation, so no inflation forecast is needed.

claims.speaker: Yoav Git
claims.quote: CTAs and in particular commodity CTAs really play into into bonds create a really nice building block for your allocation
claims.claim: CTAs, especially commodity CTAs, can be framed as part of a defensive, all-weather building block with bonds rather than only as an equity diversifier with convexity.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: in the last 70 years or so you've had as much of rising inflation as you have had falling inflation
claims.claim: Over 70 years, rising inflation periods have lasted as long as falling ones, though investors remember mostly falling or low inflation.

claims.speaker: Yoav Git
claims.quote: inflation spikes much more quickly and um and then takes a little bit longer to come down
claims.claim: Inflation spikes quickly and is stickier on the way down, so it spends more time falling; boundaries were chosen at 2% and 4.5% so each regime covers about 25% of time.

claims.speaker: Yoav Git
claims.quote: the Fed essentially overshooting um having a much more um much higher real borrowing rates
claims.claim: Since the 1970s the Fed has overshot on the way down with high real rates in order to control inflation.

claims.speaker: Yoav Git
claims.quote: falling inflation is actually kind of bad for uh commodity trend
claims.claim: Between Covid and Ukraine falling inflation was bad for commodity trend, which explains why strong commodity trends were absent until supply constraints returned.

claims.speaker: Yoav Git
claims.quote: it is really about um supply supply constraints and supply shocks um which which induce which induce uh trends
claims.claim: Trends come from supply constraints and shocks, as when low storage and a cold spell cause big natural gas trends.

claims.speaker: Yoav Git
claims.quote: the Fed is very accommodating
claims.claim: Monetary policy is relaxed, with real rates about 1%, the Fed cutting from 4.5% while CPI is above the 2% target, which is a reason to expect inflation.

claims.speaker: Yoav Git
claims.quote: financing that debt is now costing the US about a trillion a year which is enormous
claims.claim: US debt of 30 trillion now costs about 1 trillion a year in interest versus about 250 billion ten years ago, a pressure for inflation and a concern for bonds.

claims.speaker: Yoav Git
claims.quote: commodity trend what you get is something which is resilient to either environment
claims.claim: Bonds win if inflation falls and commodity trend wins if inflation rises, so the mix is resilient without forecasting inflation.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: he building this 100year portfolio if you couldn't change your portfolio for 100 years how would you build and he introduced this commodity trend
claims.claim: Commodity trend first appeared in a 100-year portfolio paper by a well-known volatility manager.

claims.speaker: Yoav Git
claims.quote: allocate just to the commodities they think about inflation and about real assets
claims.claim: Commodity-only trend is valued by allocators as a separate real-asset and inflation risk factor, so separating it from financial trend gives them choice; standalone mixing may not be more diversified.

claims.speaker: Yoav Git
claims.quote: the way I trade fixed income is slightly different to the way um we do things commodity because you have to think about the physical attributes of the asset class
claims.claim: Each asset class should be traded slightly differently since physical attributes matter in commodities and supply shocks are irrelevant in fixed income.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: a country that I've been trying to um get interested in trend following for a long time and where they have a lot of fixed income and that's Germany
claims.claim: Bonds plus commodity trend suits fixed-income-heavy institutions like Germany, but most institutions refuse anything with commodities in it.

claims.speaker: Yoav Git
claims.quote: oil this year is not the same as oil next year
claims.claim: Commodities are non-fungible across time, geography and grade (61% vs 65% iron ore), giving true diversification.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: is the mandate for you to be investing for the green transition or is the mandate for you to get pensioners in Denmark the highest possible return
claims.claim: Resistance to commodities is philosophical, not return-based; a pension's mandate is the best long-term return, so evidence should override.

claims.speaker: Yoav Git
claims.quote: we as as trend followers I mean we don't really um we don't really determine the price but what we do do is we provide liquidity in the market
claims.claim: Trend followers provide liquidity in emerging markets such as lithium contracts, where hedgers need to pre-sell production.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: most CTAs, I would argue, first of all, got long cocoa uh in early 2023
claims.claim: CTAs were long cocoa from early 2023 and sold into the 2024 rally through risk management, so they did not cause the spike.

claims.speaker: Yoav Git
claims.quote: one of the big indicators for poor performance of trend is actually oh you're trading against yourself
claims.claim: Trading against yourself is a sign of poor trend performance, so careful managers avoid markets where they are the main player.

claims.speaker: Yoav Git
claims.quote: if you think about the S&P market it's it's like 50 50 odd trillion 56 trillion I think
claims.claim: The CTA industry (about 300 billion, plus about 300 billion in QIS) is small compared with a 56 trillion equity market, but significant in some commodity markets.

claims.speaker: Yoav Git
claims.quote: up until 3 years ago fixed income really was the best asset class in terms of performance and the last three years has been a disaster
claims.claim: Fixed income was the best trend asset class until three years ago, then three poor years, though Safi, a fixed income specialist, made about 12% after fees over three years.

claims.speaker: Yoav Git
claims.quote: very few managers who have like a more generalistic and and and trend trade trend the same
claims.claim: Asset-class-specific trend trading beat generic trend run identically across asset classes in fixed income.

claims.speaker: Yoav Git
claims.quote: a lot of allocators try to time their allocation to the strategies
claims.claim: Allocators try to time allocations to strategies, which is very hard; a stable CPI+4% building block removes the need to predict inflation.

claims.speaker: Yoav Git
claims.quote: if the sharp of the underlying market is plus one you will get maybe point8 sharp into your um into your P&L of your trend following system
claims.claim: Rob Carver's blog shows a smile: trend Sharpe is about 0.8 whether the underlying Sharpe is +1 or -1, while spot-only and carry-only Sharpe do not explain trend performance.

claims.speaker: Yoav Git
claims.quote: equities are unable to essentially to harvest the underlying trend in the asset
claims.claim: Bonds, FX and metals harvest trend well, while equities cannot capture the underlying trend.

claims.speaker: Yoav Git
claims.quote: this sharp of a of a single market that we have maybe somewhere between 2 and 3 and then we diversify across our portfolio and that gives us a reduction of volatility of say 3 and a halfx
claims.claim: Single-market trend Sharpe of about 0.2 times a diversification factor of 3.5 gives a portfolio Sharpe of about 0.7.

claims.speaker: Yoav Git
claims.quote: carry just gives you this little extra, right? In terms of instead of the average being 2, the average is.3
claims.claim: Carry lifts the average single-market Sharpe from about 0.2 to 0.3, which gives about 1.05 for the portfolio.

claims.speaker: Yoav Git
claims.quote: can I tilt do we have historical reasons or fundamental under underlying reasons why we understand why there is why there is a trend
claims.claim: Tilting toward markets with structural reasons for trends (high carry, supply shocks, physical players) is justified, as including carry in the price series raises Sharpe above spot.
claims.direction: Tilt to high-carry or supply-shock markets

claims.speaker: Yoav Git
claims.quote: the trend quality the autocorrelation of the underlying price is really important
claims.claim: Trend performance depends on positive autocorrelation of the underlying price (the mathematics of trend following), not just the presence of trends.

claims.speaker: Yoav Git
claims.quote: that negative autocorrelation translates into a lower performance so you're not able to harvest as a trend follower
claims.claim: Equities show negative autocorrelation at times and horizons, so generic trend machinery earns less there.

claims.speaker: Yoav Git
claims.quote: in fixed income we see in we see actually a much higher autocorrelation
claims.claim: Fixed income shows much higher autocorrelation, so trend harvests it better.

claims.speaker: Yoav Git
claims.quote: in terms of day traders or zero day to expiry the option market
claims.claim: Autocorrelation differences arise from market structure (equity rebalancing, value traders, day traders, zero-day options) that changes over time, so trend should be adapted to structure.

claims.speaker: Yoav Git
claims.quote: how can I combine them into trend in a way that I'm still got this positive convexity
claims.claim: Trend should incorporate each market's structural characteristics (physical nature, other players) while keeping trend's convexity, without a separate model per market.

claims.speaker: Yoav Git
claims.quote: safi trades about you know let's say north of 100 150 um markets but at any one time we will actually allocate only to meaningfully to only about 50 of those
claims.claim: Safi trades 100-150 markets but allocates meaningfully to about 50 at a time, based on characteristics such as carry that make a market trend-friendly.
claims.direction: Concentrate on markets with a rate gradient

claims.speaker: Yoav Git
claims.quote: once you have different economies with different uh central banks who are trying to solve different for different things then you start getting this temperature gradients and suddenly it's becoming interesting and suddenly autocorrelation picks up
claims.claim: Developed-market FX trended poorly when rates were zero; once central banks diverge, a rate gradient creates drift and higher autocorrelation.

claims.speaker: Yoav Git
claims.quote: we started 2025 with maybe 3% between 10 year or 20 year JGBs and USD and we finished the year with like one and a half% difference
claims.claim: The JGB-US yield gap narrowed from about 3% to about 1.5% during 2025, so the yen carry opportunity will fade.

claims.speaker: Yoav Git
claims.quote: I suspect there will be carry for many many years to come
claims.claim: Bonds are about the coupon, so positive carry should persist for many years, although other asset classes have carry too.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: I think uh Japan and what's happening there and the changes there is actually much more important than people uh may realize
claims.claim: Japan's changes (rates, JGBs, carry) are more important for global markets than people realise.
